Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
212 PM EDT Thu Jul 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 232 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast. Additional 
showers and possibly a few thunderstorms will continue today but the 
threat for flooding will remain low today.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 232 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Unsettled weather to continue today with quieter weather 
expected Friday and Saturday.

2. Widespread rainfall expected on Sunday. Isolated flooding 
possible.

3. Cold frontal passage brings lingering rainfall Sunday night, 
followed by clearing and warming conditions for early to mid next 
week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 232 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The negatively tilted upper level trough will be in no 
hurry to exit the region today with the surface low pressure system 
expected to slowly slide offshore around daybreak. We will remain 
under the influence of cyclonic flow and plentiful deep layer 
moisture with PWAT values remaining in the 1.3 to 1.6 inch range. 
Cooler temperatures today will limit daytime heating and instability 
but it's plausible that we see a few breaks throughout the day, 
especially across eastern Vermont. These breaks could yield 500 J/kg 
of CAPE which would be sufficient to produce a few thunderstorms. 
The main focus on heavier precipitation today will be across the 
Connecticut River Valley which is an area that was not hit hard over 
the past 48 hours. While we remain in a marginal risk for flash 
flooding throughout the day, it's unlikely we will see the rainfall 
rates needed to yield flash flooding. Still, the slow motion of the 
storms will be concerning and will bear watching this afternoon and 
evening. 

After days of rainfall, high pressure will settle into the region 
Friday and Saturday with drier weather expected during this 
timeframe. Temperatures will warm closer to seasonal normals as we 
start to see some sunshine while dewpoints will remain in the mid 
50s to lower 60s. It's likely that we see some patchy dense fog 
Friday and Saturday mornings given a subsidence inversion and 
saturated soils from recent rainfall.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A slow moving upper level trough will move over New 
England on Sunday and is expected to take on a neutral so slightly 
negative tilt. Both the ECMWF and GFS have this transition to a 
slower moving system Sunday afternoon into the early Monday 
timeframe with the Canadian model showing a more southerly track and 
less phasing of the subtropical jet. There should be sufficient 
frontal dynamics ahead of an approaching cold front coupled with 
decent mid-level jet dynamics. In addition, deterministic guidance 
shows impressive PWAT values in the 1.7 to 1.9 inch range which is 
in the 90th + percentile. The slow moving front may yield another 
round of slow moving convection across the North Country and 
northern New York with rainfall totals in the 0.75 to 1.5 inch range 
very much in play. Depending on the motion of the storms, WPC 
believes we could see some localized 3+ inches of rainfall and have 
placed us in a marginal risk for flash flooding on Sunday. This 
system has some similarities to what we just saw across the Capital 
Region of New York and is something to watch closely for the second 
half of the upcoming weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Cold front and attendant mid-level trough should be 
progressing across the North Country from west to east Sunday night 
per consensus of 00Z NWP guidance suite. May see a few embedded 
thunderstorms with brief heavy rainfall with convective activity 
along the front. However, the good news is that this system appears 
to be relatively progressive, with the highest PoPs before midnight 
(70-80% across VT) and then exiting eastward toward daybreak on 
Monday. Depending on translation speed of the front and overall 
timing, would generally expect 0.5 to 1.0 inch rainfall most areas 
Sunday night. A clearing, drying, and warming trend is expected 
thereafter for the Monday through Wednesday time frame. Valley highs 
on Monday generally reach the lower 80s with dewpoints in the lower 
60s. Will see a gradual increase in temperatures and humidity levels 
thereafter with highs back in the mid 80s on Tuesday and in the 
upper 80s to near 90F for next Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...As a closed upper level low ambles to our 
east, an isolated shower this afternoon could affect a terminal 
or two. A combination of model and observations (satellite and 
radar) suggest MSS, and possibly MPV, will have a direct hit 
with perhaps brief reductions to MVFR, while chances are too low
at other sites to indicate in the TAF. Otherwise, some 
lingering MVFR ceilings at RUT are anticipated to scatter out 
within the next hour or so. 

Main aviation impacts will be related to high probabilities of 
fog development tonight given recent rain and light boundary 
layer flow amidst mainly clear skies as high pressure builds in 
from the west. While the high will not be directly overhead and 
will be coming in from the southwest rather than northwest, 
favorable factors for fog development include the moist low 
level air in place with crossover temperatures in the low to mid
60s and lack of dry air advection tonight. As such, have 
favored dense fog development for much of the overnight hours 
at MPV and SLK, and towards daybreak at RUT. MSS will also have 
at least intervals of fog and BTV may see a brief period of fog 
make it to the runway around sunrise. With relatively little 
recent rain at EFK and less consistent radiational fog 
development climatologically, have only indicated BR at this 
time at this site. 

Aside from modest north winds at BTV and PBG near 10 knots this
afternoon, winds will be light/terrain driven through the 
period, with a tendency to be from the northwest after 12Z.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Definite SHRA,
Chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.
Monday Night: VFR/MVFR conditions possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
